objects.taxonomy_description: Domestic cat with a distinctive grey or tawny coat mottled with black in a tabby pattern. Coat features characteristic M-shaped marking on the forehead, dark stripes along the body, and ringed tail. Pattern types include classic (swirled), mackerel (striped), spotted, or ticked. Body is medium-sized, well-proportioned, and muscular. Head is round with a short muzzle. Ears are medium-sized, pointed, and erect. Eyes are large, round, and green, gold, or copper. The breed's signature features include the distinctive tabby pattern with M forehead marking and striped legs.

objects.taxonomy_description: Stringed instrument with solid or semi-hollow body (no sound hole required). Body shape varies: Stratocaster (double-cutaway, contoured edges), Les Paul (single-cutaway, carved top), Telecaster (single-cutaway, slab body). Body is wood (alder, mahogany, maple) with glossy polyester or nitrocellulose finish in solid colors, sunburst, or natural wood grain. Neck is maple or mahogany with fretted fingerboard (rosewood or maple, 21-24 frets). Pickups (magnetic, 1-3) mounted on body. Control knobs (volume, tone) and pickup selector switch. Bridge is fixed or tremolo. Headstock has 6 tuning pegs. Cable jack on body edge.

objects.taxonomy_description: Uncastrated adult male sheep measuring 65-110 cm at withers weighing 35-180 kg. Body covered with dense woolly fleece in white, brown, or black. Head broad with laterally spiraling horns (in horned breeds). Horns thick and ridged. Eyes dark with horizontal rectangular pupils. Ears lateral and drooping. Neck thick and muscular. Body compact and stocky. Legs sturdy with cloven hooves. Tail short. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, wool insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Secondary sexual characteristics include larger size and prominent horns.
